global_caption: The video contains 5 shots and is a warm-toned realistic origami tutorial. It primarily uses natural light from the window and soft fill lighting, resulting in a warm, clean visual aesthetic with steady, controlled camera movement. The The emotional tone remains consistently gentle and focused throughout.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a steady eye-level wide shot that slowly pushes in. A wooden table by the window is positioned slightly below center, creating a balanced composition. In the foreground, a neat tabletop holds several sheets of colored paper. The background features a window frame illuminated by warm sunlight and softly blurred indoor corners. The focus rests on the upper body of a young woman and the props on the table. She wears a natural smile, holding up a completed paper crane with her left hand and displaying a square sheet of colored paper with her right. The camera slowly moves forward, allowing viewers to clearly see the proportion between the material and the finished product. The paper gently trembles at her fingertips, and soft highlights form along the crease edges under the light.
shot2: The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one, transitioning to an overhead close-up. The wooden grain of the tabletop spreads horizontally as a clear background, with a tight composition where the colored paper dominates the frame. In shallow depth of field, the hands and edges of the paper are most sharply defined. She carefully folds the square sheet of colored paper along its diagonal, slowly aligning the two corners and then pressing down from the center toward both ends with her fingertips to create a crisp crease, while softly explaining “先沿对角线对折，对齐四角，再把中间的折痕压实”. Warm natural light slants in from the upper left of the frame, casting shadows along the fold that help viewers perceive the structural change.
shot3: The third shot enters with a sharp cut from the previous one, using an overhead close-up with a slightly wider framing to fully capture the unfolding motion of both hands. The composition uses the central axis of the paper as a visual guide. The paper transitions from a triangular shape into a more three-dimensional diamond structure, while the Chinese The camera follows her hand movements with a subtle downward tracking motion, ensuring that each alignment, pinch, and smoothing action remains in focus.
shot4: Shot 4 connects to the previous shot with a soft, continuous motion cut, transitioning to a level close-up from a front-side angle that captures the crucial steps in forming the paper crane into a three-dimensional shape. In the foreground, her fingers steadily support the body of the paper crane, with focus placed on the tip and the crease junctions. The background window light is softly blurred into warm highlights. As she folds, she quietly explains in Chinese “现在把一端翻出颈部，另一端翻出尾部，折的时候慢一点，角度尽量对称”, gently pinching the lower part of the paper and pulling apart while flipping both ends in opposite directions, gradually creating a difference in length between the neck and tail sections. The camera performs a slight lateral pan and a subtle push-in, emphasizing the opening, folding, and shaping of the paper layers. Sharp creases become more pronounced under pressure, with clear and detailed movements shown without any skipped steps.
shot5: Shot 5 concludes with a soft fade-in/fade-out transition from the previous shot, using a close-up pull-back to capture the young woman returning naturally to her wooden desk by the window. The composition begins with her finished paper crane in hand, initially focusing on the crane's head and wings, then gradually pulling back to include her posture as she holds it up along with the tabletop. She gently spreads the wings fully, allowing the silhouette of the paper crane to unfold completely, then lifts it to chest height with both hands, smiling as she summarizes in Chinese “最后把翅膀轻轻展开，一只纸鹤就完成了，跟着步骤慢慢做就可以”. As the camera pulls back, viewers get a full view of the final result and the working environment.
